proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(\pi_i=P_{\vartheta}(U=i)\) for \(i\in\{1,2,3,4\}\). By binary response-type consistency, the event \(Y=1\) under \(X=1\) occurs exactly for response types \(1\) and \(2\), whereas under \(X=0\) it occurs exactly for response types \(1\) and \(3\). The local independence \(X\perp U\) therefore gives
\[
P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)=\pi_1+\pi_2,
\qquad
P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=0)=\pi_1+\pi_3.
\]
The local restriction \(P_{\vartheta}(U=3)=0\) is \(\pi_3=0\), so subtraction yields
\[
P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)-P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=0)=\pi_2.
\]
Because \(\vartheta\in\mathcal F_A(p,m)\), its selected conditional table is \(p\). Selected-table positivity gives \(r_{11}>0\) and \(r_{00}>0\). Since \(S=1\) almost surely,
\[
P_{\vartheta}(X=1,Y=1)=r_{11}>0,
\qquad
P_{\vartheta}(X=0,Y=0)=r_{00}>0.
\]
Consequently \(P_{\vartheta}(X=1)>0\), \(P_{\vartheta}(X=0)>0\), and the two denominators in the statement are positive. For necessity, response consistency says that among types compatible with \((X,Y)=(1,1)\), precisely type \(2\) is the necessity type. Using \(X\perp U\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{PN}(\vartheta)
&=P_{\vartheta}(U=2\mid X=1,Y=1)\\
&=\frac{P_{\vartheta}(U=2,Y=1\mid X=1)}{P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)}
=\frac{\pi_2}{\pi_1+\pi_2}\\
&=\frac{P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)-P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=0)}{P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)}.
\end{aligned}
\]
For sufficiency, under \(X=0\) the event \(Y=0\) occurs exactly for types \(2\) and \(4\). Hence, again by \(X\perp U\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{PS}(\vartheta)
&=P_{\vartheta}(U=2\mid X=0,Y=0)\\
&=\frac{P_{\vartheta}(U=2,Y=0\mid X=0)}{P_{\vartheta}(Y=0\mid X=0)}
=\frac{\pi_2}{\pi_2+\pi_4}\\
&=\frac{P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)-P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=0)}{P_{\vartheta}(Y=0\mid X=0)}.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves the displayed identity for the particular restricted SCM \(\vartheta\). By definition of the design-A target set and \(\vartheta\in\mathcal F_A(p,m)\), one has \(\tau(\vartheta)\in\mathcal T_A(p,m)\). Therefore, if \(\lvert\mathcal T_A(p,m)\rvert=1\), its unique element must equal \(\tau(\vartheta)\), and thus equals the displayed pair. No converse inclusion or rigidity conclusion was used.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Validation corollary (published Tian--Pearl sanity check). Let \(\vartheta\in\mathcal F_A(p,m)\). Suppose, locally for this \(\vartheta\), that \(S=1\) almost surely, \(X\perp U\) under \(P_{\vartheta}\), and \(P_{\vartheta}(U=3)=0\). Then
\[
\tau(\vartheta)=\left(
\frac{P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)-P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=0)}{P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)},
\frac{P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)-P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=0)}{P_{\vartheta}(Y=0\mid X=0)}
\right),
\]
where both denominators are strictly positive. If, in addition, \(\lvert\mathcal T_A(p,m)\rvert=1\), then the unique element of \(\mathcal T_A(p,m)\) is the displayed pair. These local hypotheses do not imply rigidity of the unrestricted design-A fiber and are not assumptions on either main design.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frozen claim incorrectly attributed a per-SCM randomized-monotone calculation to an unrestricted atlas value and did not state that the displayed SCM belongs to the design-A fiber. The replacement states the calculation for a specified compatible SCM and invokes the design-A target set only under a separate singleton hypothesis.

proposed.statement:
Validation corollary (published Tian--Pearl sanity check). Let \(\vartheta\in\mathcal F_A(p,m)\). Suppose, locally for this \(\vartheta\), that \(S=1\) almost surely, \(X\perp U\) under \(P_{\vartheta}\), and \(P_{\vartheta}(U=3)=0\). Then
\[
\tau(\vartheta)=\left(
\frac{P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)-P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=0)}{P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)},
\frac{P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)-P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=0)}{P_{\vartheta}(Y=0\mid X=0)}
\right),
\]
where both denominators are strictly positive. If, in addition, \(\lvert\mathcal T_A(p,m)\rvert=1\), then the unique element of \(\mathcal T_A(p,m)\) is the displayed pair. These local hypotheses do not imply rigidity of the unrestricted design-A fiber and are not assumptions on either main design.
proposed.justification: This validation corollary checks the response-type parameterization against the published Tian--Pearl formulas on one explicitly restricted compatible SCM; it does not supply rigidity.
proposed.gap: Tian and Pearl (2000) already establish the benchmark. The only local task is to derive the same formulas for the specified design-A SCM and distinguish that identity from singleton identification of the full target set.
proposed.consumer: Implementers can use the formulas as a per-SCM regression check and may compare them with the unique design-A target only after singleton rigidity has independently been certified.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The corrected claim removes the full-atlas and cycle-lift dependencies and adds the design-A fiber and singleton-rigidity definitions actually used by the proof.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Necessity and sufficiency of the proposed finite structural atlas on every mixed-support design-A and design-B fiber.
open_obligations.obstruction: The theorem depends on the unresolved mixed-support elimination question, which is not owned by this solve unit. The established rank-two orientation boxes and residual-margin forest do not prove that the proposed inactive-row, coincident-endpoint, and algebraic-root charts exhaust every real component and support face. Generic two-copy quantifier elimination would decide target constancy but would not prove the claimed structural classifier.
open_obligations.attempted: Extended the established cycle-to-SCM lift, the all-rank-two orientation classification, and the conditional residual-forest elimination to the theorem's two completed branches; audited whether their chart arguments cover rank-one and inactive-row degeneracies, where the missing component-exhaustion step remains.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The established cycle-to-SCM lift gives the exact image equalities
\[
\mathcal T_A(p,m)=\{\tau_C(b,a):(b,a)\in\mathcal C_A(T)\},
\qquad
\mathcal T_B(p)=\{\tau_C(b,a):(b,a,m,g,\pi)\in\mathcal C_B(T)\}.
\]
Thus any two cycle points with different \(\tau_C\) lift to legal full SCM twins, including on boundary faces; strict positivity is required only for interior faces. The established all-rank-two design-A theorem supplies exact oriented endpoint boxes and a necessary-and-sufficient agreement test there. The established design-B residual theorem eliminates the positive unknown margins, conditional on \((b,a,\rho)\), by negative residual proportionality, forest scale propagation, cycle products, normalization, and the relevance inequality. These arguments prove the claimed conclusion on those branches. They do not show that the proposed mixed-support chart list exhausts every real component and support face of either full cycle fiber.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Universal coverage of every singular and boundary observable law by the same global structural atlas.
open_obligations.obstruction: Agreement with the published regular formula and the already-certified all-rank-two boundary datum are available, but the theorem's universal boundary clause is equivalent to the unresolved exhaustiveness of the mixed-support chart list.
open_obligations.attempted: Matched the regular published PN/PS functional to the cycle target through the established lift, separated the certified forced-zero rank-two boundary branch, and used the residual-forest theorem for the conditional design-B margin problem.
open_obligations.partial_result: On the regular domain of Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki, the cited identification result makes the Appendix expressions (A.28)--(A.33) equal the causal PN/PS pair. The cycle-to-SCM lift preserves that pair as \(\tau_C\); hence, whenever the corresponding full target set is a singleton, its element equals the published expression. Independently, the established rank-two boundary theorem and the established explicit boundary calculation classify the forced-zero datum \(p^{\mathrm{bd}}\), while the residual-forest theorem gives an exact conditional elimination of design-B margins. What remains unproved is the universal assertion that the stated structural charts cover every rank-loss, coincident-endpoint, inactive-row, and mixed-support law.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Attribution of the unique design-B overlap value to the unfinished global compiler on every Kawakami-regular law.
open_obligations.obstruction: Kawakami's simultaneous equations identify the conditional response-type weights, and the explicit boundary singularity is proved, but the statement still asserts output by the global atlas, whose mixed-support exhaustiveness is unresolved.
open_obligations.attempted: Derived the PN/PS transformation from response consistency and verified exact column dependence of both explicit proxy-loading matrices; retained the already-established singleton boundary calculation.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The cited Kawakami theorem identifies \(\omega_0^{\mathrm K}\) and \(\omega_1^{\mathrm K}\) under \(\mathcal K_{\mathrm K}\). Response consistency then gives directly
\[
\tau(\vartheta)=\phi_{\mathrm K}(\omega_0^{\mathrm K},\omega_1^{\mathrm K}).
\]
For the explicit boundary endpoints, every row of \(A_x^{\mathrm K}(b^{\mathrm{bd}})\) is \((1,b_i(w_1),b_i(w_2),b_i(w_3))\), and normalization of \(b_i\) implies that the first column is the sum of the final three columns. Therefore \(A_x^{\mathrm K}(b^{\mathrm{bd}})\) is singular for \(x=0,1\). The established boundary theorem gives
\[
\mathcal F_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})\ne\varnothing,
\qquad
\mathcal T_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})=\{(1/2,1/2)\}.
\]
This proves the one-law scope separation. Only the attribution of a returned value to the unfinished global compiler remains unavailable.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Termination, chart-count, algebraic-degree, and rational certificate-size bounds for the specific structural compiler.
open_obligations.obstruction: The compiler's mixed-support chart enumeration has not been completed, so its chart count and algebraic degrees cannot yet be bounded. A generic real-algebraic decision bound applies to the raw fiber but does not certify the theorem's promised structural method.
open_obligations.attempted: Counted variables, constraints, and degrees in the fixed-alphabet raw cycle systems, bounded generic real-algebraic decision, and isolated the terminating rank-two and residual-forest branches.
open_obligations.partial_result: For fixed \(k=\lvert\mathcal Z\rvert\) and \(\ell=\lvert\mathcal W\rvert\), the raw normalized cycle systems contain only finitely many polynomial equalities and weak or strict inequalities, with degree at most two before residual proportionality is eliminated. After deleting redundant simplex coordinates, their variable and constraint counts are bounded by \(C_0(k\ell+k+\ell)\) for a universal \(C_0\). Consequently generic fixed-dimensional real-algebraic decision and sampling give a terminating doubly exponential envelope, and the established all-rank-two structural branch terminates by finite orientation enumeration, linear algebra, and order tests over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\). The residual-forest argument likewise eliminates its margin block by finitely many ratio and cycle tests. This does not establish the claimed bounds for \(\mathscr A\), because its mixed-support structural chart enumeration has not been completed, and replacing it by generic two-copy quantifier elimination would contradict the theorem's stated classification method.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Unconditional correctness of the deterministic chart selector for the claimed atlas on every separated rigid stratum.
open_obligations.obstruction: The multinomial delta-method calculation closes once the incident atlas is locally exhaustive. Without the mixed-support exhaustion theorem, an omitted nearby component can invalidate chart certification and the exclusion of incompatible charts.
open_obligations.attempted: Completed the chart-distance, slack-continuity, common-Jacobian Taylor, sandwich-consistency, positive-definiteness, Wald, and fallback calculations conditional on local atlas exhaustiveness.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Conditional on local exhaustiveness of the certified finite atlas, independent multinomial sampling and proportional independent margin sampling give
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta)\Rightarrow N(0,\Omega_{\zeta}),
\qquad
\widehat\Omega_n\xrightarrow{P}\Omega_{\zeta}.
\]
For every incident chart,
\[
d_{\chi}(\widehat\zeta_n)\le \lVert\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta\rVert_2=O_P(n^{-1/2})=o_P(t_n),
\]
and continuity of \(\eta_{\chi}\), together with \(\eta_{\chi}(\zeta)\ge\varepsilon\), makes its slack test pass with probability tending to one. Positive distance from incompatible chart closures excludes those charts. The common incident value and Jacobian then imply
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_n-\tau)
=J_{\chi}(\zeta)\sqrt n(\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta)+o_P(1),
\]
uniformly on compact subsets of the separated stratum. Continuity of the sandwich map and \(\lambda_{\min}(V_{\tau})\ge\varepsilon\) give covariance consistency, eventual certification, and ordinary Wald coverage. The fallback identities follow directly from their definitions. This proves the asymptotic calculation conditional on atlas exhaustiveness but cannot establish selector correctness if a mixed-support chart is missing.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The uniform first-order Hausdorff equivalence between the exact confidence-fiber inversion and the selected Wald ellipse for the globally defined atlas.
open_obligations.obstruction: Exact finite-sample coverage is independent of rank stability, but the Hausdorff assertion needs a uniform glued-chart likelihood expansion and proof that no mixed-support component is omitted near the true law.
open_obligations.attempted: Proved finite-sample Berger--Boos coverage from the preliminary-region event and exact super-uniform tail values, and reduced the local separated smooth case to the profile-Wald quadratic conditional on atlas exhaustiveness.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Let \(q_0\) denote the true observable law and \(t_0=\tau(\vartheta)\). Exact inversion of each binomial tail and the stated Bonferroni allocation give
\[
P_{q_0}(q_0\notin C_n)\le\beta_n.
\]
For fixed compatible \((q,t)\), define
\[
G_{q,t}=P_q\{\Delta_n^{\mathrm{rep}}(t)\ge\Delta_n^{\mathrm{obs}}(t)\}.
\]
The upper-tail value is super-uniform, including at atoms: \(P_q(G_{q,t}\le u)\le u\) for \(u\in[0,1]\). Since \(t_0\in\mathcal T(q_0)\), on \(\{q_0\in C_n\}\) the supremum in \(\operatorname{pv}_n(t_0)\) includes \(q_0\). Hence
\[
\operatorname{pv}_n(t_0)\ge \min\{1,\beta_n+G_{q_0,t_0}\},
\]
and, because \(\beta_n\le\alpha/2\),
\[
P_{q_0}\{t_0\notin K_n\}
\le \beta_n+P_{q_0}\{G_{q_0,t_0}\le\alpha-\beta_n\}
\le\alpha.
\]
This exact finite-sample argument is valid along arbitrary sequences approaching \(\mathfrak D\). On a locally exhaustive separated smooth chart, the multinomial likelihood has the usual uniform quadratic expansion and the common incident Jacobian reduces the target profile to the Wald quadratic, yielding \(\sqrt n\,d_{\mathrm H}(K_n,W_n)\to0\) in probability. The asserted global Hausdorff conclusion still requires proof that no nearby mixed-support component has been omitted and a uniform glued-chart profile expansion.

prose_updates.honest_scope: The central open content is Open-ended Question 1, and the proposal is field-tier. The proposed theorem permits coefficient-field algebraic outputs and requires strict-positive twins only for interior nonrigid strata. Integer-polynomial certificates and bit bounds require explicitly encoded rational observables. Population-margin positivity is not maintained independently: every compatible law with positive selected cells and \(c=P(S=1)>0\) satisfies it, while design-A margins remain supplied observables. The chart evaluator, estimator, covariance output, and reported region are total; absence of a certified separated rigid chart triggers the declared numerical and full-square fallbacks. Covariance consistency and Wald coverage are asserted only for first-order-compatible charts separated from incompatible chart closures, with twice continuously differentiable extensions, proportional margin sampling when needed, and target covariance bounded away from singularity. Confidence-fiber inversion provides honest coverage at every transition; first-order Hausdorff agreement with Wald is asserted only on separated regular strata, and no shrinking-diameter assertion is made at genuinely unidentified laws. The Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki and Shingaki--Kuroki statements are supporting overlap-agreement and boundary-coverage checks, not comparative extension claims. Kawakami's no-selection IV-plus-proxy result is compared through its Figure 2(b), equation (2), and Theorem 1(i)--(iii): agreement is claimed only on the common regular scope, and the explicit selected boundary datum supplies only a strict scope separation through failure of \(A_x\) invertibility. Neither theorem is claimed to subsume or extend the other. The Shu--Wang--Li compatible-model polytope and the selected proxy-cycle fiber encode different information, so no subsumption claim is made. Known-selection reweighting is an implementation normalization. The Tian--Pearl validation applies to a specified \(\vartheta\in\mathcal F_A(p,m)\) satisfying locally \(S=1\) almost surely, \(X\perp U\), and \(P_{\vartheta}(U=3)=0\); it proves the classical formulas for \(\tau(\vartheta)\), and identifies them with the unique element of \(\mathcal T_A(p,m)\) only when singleton rigidity is separately assumed. These local restrictions neither prove rigidity nor constrain either main design. The GEUVADIS analysis certifies consequences conditional on the stated proxy, exclusion, selection, and IV assumptions; population labels and genotype variables do not empirically prove those assumptions.
